document.title: Pakistan: Ambassador Raises bin Laden with Foreign Secretary Shamshad Ahmed (Islama 07510)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] Ambassador William Milam tells Pakistan's Foreign Secretary that, despite other sticking points such as the status of women, the presence of bin Laden and his organization in Afghanistan is the one issue with no flexibility. He asks for Pakistan's help, stressing that U.S. patience is thin and that it needs a settlement in days rather than weeks. Excised.

persons.name: Osama bin Laden
persons.role: Leader of an organization based in Afghanistan; US demanded his extradition

mentions.quote: OUR PARAMOUNT INTEREST IN AFGHANISTAN AT THE PRESENT TIME WAS TO SECURE THE IMMEDIATE EXTRADITION OF BIN LADEN FROM THE COUNTRY.
IN AN OCTOBER 5 MEETING WITH FOREIGN SECRETARY SHAMSHAD AHMED ON ANOTHER SUBJECT, AMBASSADOR BRIEFLY RAISED THE ISSUE OF OSAMA BIN LADEN.
CLASSIFIED BY AMBASSADOR WILLIAM B. MILAM.

events.description: Ambassador Milam raised bin Laden with Foreign Secretary Shamshad Ahmed, urging rapid action and extradition from Afghanistan.
Ambassador discussed bin Laden with the Pakistani Prime Minister the previous week.
Ambassador Milam raised bin Laden with Foreign Secretary Shamshad Ahmed, urging Pakistan's help and stressing US patience was thin and a settlement was needed within days.
Milam discussed bin Laden with the Pakistani Prime Minister the previous week.
Embassy Islamabad cable 07510 sent to State reporting the Shamshad conversation and a pending request for a Prime Minister meeting.

key_claims: In Oct 1998 the US told Pakistan its paramount interest in Afghanistan was the immediate extradition of bin Laden.
The US said it had no flexibility on the presence of bin Laden and his organization in Afghanistan.
The US was seeking a dialogue with the Taliban with limited success.
US urged Pakistan to settle the matter within days, saying patience was wearing thin.
The US sought to prevent an Iran–Taliban conflict.
